row.convention: CMS Medicare Beneficiary Identifier hyphenated display convention
row.description: The Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI) is commonly displayed as three groups separated by hyphens, such as 1EG4-TE5-MK73, for Medicare insurance eligibility and claims administration.

neighbors.distinction: The older HICN convention can contain a claim-account suffix and is not an MBI.
An NPI is a 10-digit provider identifier rather than a beneficiary identifier.

row.wrong_generalization: Treating the hyphens as optional because some system-to-system payloads omit display punctuation, or assuming every 11-character insurance identifier is an MBI.

row.description: Certificates of Liability Insurance identify the ACORD 25 form and may include an optional parenthesized edition revision, for example ACORD 25 (2016/03).

neighbors.distinction: The issue date identifies when a particular certificate was produced.
The effective date begins policy coverage and is unrelated to the ACORD form edition.

row.wrong_generalization: Requiring an edition mark on every certificate, or treating the edition date as the certificate issuance date.

row.convention: ANSI X12 835 Claim Adjustment Segment (CAS) convention
row.description: In an ANSI X12 835 remittance advice, a CAS segment carries an adjustment group code followed by one or more repeated claim-adjustment reason, amount, and quantity sections.

neighbors.distinction: CLP communicates claim-level payment information rather than adjustment reasons.
An 837 claim may carry CAS information, but its transaction context and usage differ from an 835 remittance.

row.wrong_generalization: Assuming a CAS segment contains only one adjustment, or parsing repeated adjustment triples as independent segments.

row.description: A claim reference number is carrier-assigned and is commonly recorded on loss notices, claim correspondence, and policy servicing systems. Samples often appear to have one fixed width even though insurers use varying internal lengths.

neighbors.distinction: A policy number identifies a contract or policy term rather than a reported loss.
A claimant identifier identifies a person or organization associated with the claim, not the claim file itself.

row.wrong_generalization: Inferring a fixed ten-digit width from a sample file, or assuming a numeric claim reference can be validated without the issuing carrier's system.
